transcript: Organ donation doesn't really feel like the most obvious choice for a musical, at least on paper. But the heart really won me over. It actually occurred to me while watching the show that while the inner workings of a hospital is something that has been very explored in other mediums, particularly TV, we don't really have any musicals that tackle it. Which is kind of surprising, given that I think musicals are at their best when emotions are running high. And I can think of very few places on earth where emotions are as high as they are at hospitals. And I think the heart specifically really takes full advantage of this, musicalizing the highs and lows of a heart transplant. But I also love that they chose to go for this EDM Electro pop score. For one, it's a sound that we don't really hear in musical theatre all that often. But two, it's also a genre of music that is very beat focused. And so it really lends itself well to lining up with things like heartbeats, the beeping of medical equipment and just the overall pulsing of a hospital operating like this well oiled machine. It's very, very smart. Now, the show is juggling a lot of different characters, brought together by a really stellar ensemble of actors. You, of course, have the two patients involved in the heart transplant, You have their families, and you have all of the medical professionals facilitating This process. and I do think this is probably the biggest weakness of the show. With only a 90 minute run time, they don't really have the time to fully flesh out these characters. They try their best to give each character these little humanizing moments where we'll get a glimpse into, like, their hobbies or what they're like outside of work, but it's not always effective. And this is one area where I think the T V Procedural has an advantage, because there you have episodes and episodes to get to know all of these characters that work in the hospital, whereas here we are meeting everyone for the first and last time. But on the flip side, I do think that the show does a pretty good job at painting this comprehensive view of the entire process, from organ donation through to the actual transplant itself. And as someone who doesn't watch a lot of TV Shows, I found it to be genuinely educational, not just for learning about the process, but also making a pretty strong case for just how important organ donation is, but in a way that rarely feels preachy. I actually think it will be perfect for school groups. And overall, this is definitely going to be a Broadway Ben recommendation. It's not a perfect musical, but it is a pretty novel one. And the stuff that it does well, I think it does really well. And at the very least, you'll Probably learn something new.
reasoning: Ben explicitly gives it a 'Broadway Ben recommendation' and praises the novel concept, EDM score, and ensemble, while noting the character development weakness due to runtime. Clear recommendation with caveats puts it solidly in Positive.
